definition: Darkforest is a computer go program developed by Meta Platforms, based on deep learning techniques using a convolutional neural network.
details: Its updated version Darkfores2 combines the techniques of its predecessor with Monte Carlo tree search. The MCTS effectively takes tree search methods commonly seen in computer chess programs and randomizes them. With the update, the system is known as Darkfmcts3. Darkforest is of similar strength to programs like CrazyStone and Zen. It has been tested against a professional human player at the 2016 UEC cup. Google's AlphaGo program won against a professional player in October 2015 using a similar combination of techniques. Darkforest is named after Liu Cixin's science fiction novel The Dark Forest.

explainer.lead: Darkforest is Meta Platforms’ deep-learning program for playing Go, built around a convolutional neural network. Its later versions add Monte Carlo tree search, combining learned board evaluation with randomized exploration of possible continuations.

tiers.eli5: Darkforest is a computer player for Go that learned from patterns on the board, a bit like recognizing shapes in a picture. Its newer version also tries out different possible futures of the game before choosing a move. Its name comes from Liu Cixin’s science fiction novel The Dark Forest.
tiers.practitioner: Treat Darkforest as the convolutional-neural-network baseline and Darkfmcts3 as the system combining that approach with Monte Carlo tree search. Its playing strength was comparable to CrazyStone and Zen, and its test against a professional at the 2016 UEC Cup should not be read as equivalent to AlphaGo’s professional win.
tiers.paperLevel: Darkforest applies a convolutional neural network to computer Go; Darkfores2 augments this learned component with Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS), with the updated system called Darkfmcts3. MCTS introduces randomized tree-search exploration rather than exhaustively enumerating the game tree. Reported strength is comparable to CrazyStone and Zen, while AlphaGo had already defeated a professional player in October 2015 using a similar combination of techniques.

explainer.example: During a Go game, Darkfmcts3 starts from the current board, applies Darkforest’s neural-network techniques, and uses randomized Monte Carlo tree search to explore possible future sequences before playing a move. The original Darkforest lacks that added search component.

explainer.intuition: Playing Go requires both recognizing useful patterns on the board and considering how a game might unfold. Darkforest supplies the learned pattern recognition, while its update adds randomized search through possible continuations.
howItWorks: Take the current Go board as the program’s input.
Use a convolutional neural network to apply deep learning to the board position.
In Darkfores2, combine those techniques with Monte Carlo tree search to explore possible continuations randomly.
Use the combined system, known as Darkfmcts3, to choose a move.
explainer.whyItMatters: Darkforest illustrates the combination of deep convolutional networks and tree search in computer Go, an approach also used by AlphaGo. Its professional-player test and comparable strength to CrazyStone and Zen place it among the notable programs of that period.
misconceptions: Darkforest is not AlphaGo; AlphaGo defeated a professional player in October 2015 using a similar combination of techniques.
Darkfores2 and Darkfmcts3 refer to the updated line of the same project, not unrelated Go programs.
Being tested against a professional at the 2016 UEC Cup does not itself establish that Darkforest won.
